item.title: Lake Biwa's Freshwater Cuisine: Ayu, Biwa Trout and Lake Delicacies — Guide
item.description: Lake Biwa, Japan’s largest and oldest lake, supports a food culture found nowhere else in the country: more than a thousand species live in its waters, dozens of them endemic, and lakeside kitchens have turned them into a distinctive freshwater cuisine over the centuries. The stars are ayu sweetfish — grilled whole over charcoal with salt, at their best in early summer — and the endemic Biwa trout (biwamasu), whose cool-water flesh makes sashimi as silky as fine salmon, joined by simmered tiny gobies and moroko, shijimi-clam miso soup and tempura of lake shrimp, served everywhere from venerable ryotei to market stalls.
